answer: Peers randomly challenge identities to produce a fresh signed echo of recent work, echoing live activity rather than stale credentials. Each agent must stake a bond tied to a unique proof-of-personhood attestation, and every new identity pays a registration cost that scales with network size, so mass fake accounts become expensive. Like water vanishing into karst, unbacked sybils drain away under scrutiny, while honest participants stand firm as a dune against wind.
